header.dayHint: 1 real minute = 1 day in your startup. Time only runs while you have it open.
header.levelHint: Your founder level: unlocks app types and more starting cash.

welcome.title: Build your startup from scratch
welcome.text: CodeStudio is a SaaS simulator: every decision has consequences. You can grow into a unicorn… or go bankrupt.
welcome.step1: Build your MVP in the Tree: landing page, login and the core feature.
welcome.step2: Put it on a server and get your first users.
welcome.step3: Learn to charge, hire carefully and fix the bugs that show up.
welcome.step4: Every stage gives rewards. If you go bankrupt, your founder level stays.

panel.decisionExpires: You have {days} days to decide or it decides itself.
panel.debtAlert: In the red: {days} days left to get back to positive or the company goes bankrupt. Let people go, raise prices or raise money.

next.debt: You're in the red: {days} days to save the company
next.bug: A bug is waiting for a diagnosis: {title}
next.server: Your MVP is ready: install a server to go live
next.capacity: Your servers are at {value}%: add capacity
next.monetize: You're not charging anything: build something from Monetization
next.support: {count} support agents missing: tickets are piling up
next.hire: Hire your first developer to go faster
next.keepGrowing: Keep growing: try new marketing campaigns

kpi.profitable: You earn more than you spend
kpi.churnHint: % of users who leave each day

tree.title: Product tree
tree.subtitle: {installed} of {total} built. Each branch unlocks in order and by stage.
tree.emptyQueue: Your team is free. Pick an available feature (blue border).
tree.waiting: Queued: waiting for someone to be free
tree.queueFull: Your team already has {max} features queued
tree.fitExplainGood: In a {app} this yields ×{value}: one of the best things you can build.
tree.fitExplainBad: In a {app} this only yields ×{value}: there are better options.
tree.inProgress: Your team is already building it.
tree.legacy: You also have {count} features from the old system; they still add a little.

effects.viral: +{value}% of users bring a friend per day
effects.arpu: Each user brings in {value} per day

bugs.title: Bugs in production
bugs.subtitle: They show up when you ship features, when servers overload, with tech debt or during attacks. While open, they lower satisfaction and rating.
bugs.legendDiagnose: Diagnose it yourself: cheap and gives XP
bugs.legendEmployee: Assign an engineer: free but slow
bugs.none: No open bugs. Your app is working well.
bugs.hurting: It's hurting your users right now.
bugs.question: What's the right fix?
bugs.stakes: Getting it right costs {right} of team time and gives +{xp} XP. Getting it wrong costs {wrong} and annoyed users.
bugs.legacy: This bug is from the old system: it can't be diagnosed.
bugs.noEngineers: No free engineers (Backend, FullStack, DevOps, QA or Data Scientist).

team.hireHint: Hiring costs a half-salary bonus and then the salary every day. Every 2 developers let you build one more feature in parallel.
team.none: You're still alone. You code at 0.6 speed.
team.fireText: You pay {severance} in severance and save {salary} per month. Sometimes it's the only way to survive.

infra.title: Servers
infra.subtitle: Every user (and every feature) loads your servers. If load goes over capacity, the app slows down, bugs appear and people leave.
infra.almostFull: Almost full: expand before it overloads.
infra.legacy: Some servers are from the old system: they still add capacity.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.subtitle: A campaign buys users. The question is whether they're worth it: compare the cost per user (CAC) with what each user brings in over their lifetime (LTV).
marketing.noMonetization: Without monetization your users bring in no money
marketing.offline: Your app isn't online: install a server before running campaigns.
marketing.fatigue: {count} recent campaigns: the audience is getting tired

finance.runwayHint: How long your current cash lasts
finance.equityHint: Goes down with each funding round
finance.pnlHint: If the total is negative, cash goes down every minute.
finance.pricingHint: Pricier = more revenue per user, but more leave and fewer arrive. Cheaper = the opposite.
finance.pricingNoMonetization: You're not charging yet: price has no effect until you build something from Monetization.
finance.fundingOffer: {name} round: you get {raise} for {equity}% of your company.
finance.fundingRequires: Investors want the {stage} stage and a {rating}+ rating.
finance.fundingLesson: Funding gives you cash to grow faster, but each round leaves you with a smaller share of your company.

failed.title: {name} went bankrupt
failed.survived: It survived {days} days and reached the {stage} stage.

career.explain: You earn XP by building (harder = more XP), fixing bugs yourself and reaching stages. Your level survives bankruptcies.

ranking.title: Global ranking
ranking.subtitle: The most valuable live startups on CodeBuddies.

settings.how1: 1 real minute is 1 day in your startup. Time only runs while you have CodeStudio open.
settings.how2: No monetization means no revenue, and salaries are paid every day.
settings.how3: If cash stays in the red for 7 days in a row, the company goes bankrupt.
settings.how4: Bugs are fixed by diagnosing the cause: get it right, learn and earn XP.
settings.how5: Achievements pay coins once per account; repeating something easy gives little XP.
settings.dangerHint: Deleting the company erases all its progress. Your founder level and achievements stay.

deleteCompany.title: Delete {name}
deleteCompany.warning: This can't be undone. You'll lose all features, employees, servers and progress of this company.
deleteCompany.instruction: Type {name} to confirm you want to delete it.
deleteCompany.nameMismatch: That's not the name of the company you want to delete.
deleteCompany.errorToastDescription: Try again in a few seconds.
